claims.text: A density-functional-theory method incorporating phonon-phonon interactions can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed method will reduce mean absolute prediction error by at least 15% relative to current predictions.
The target materials are high-entropy alloys in the as-cast state.
The approach uses ab initio phonon-dispersion calculations based on density functional theory and phonon-phonon interactions.
The proposed tests cover operating temperatures from 300 K to 1000 K.
The approach is intended for alloys containing at least five principal elements.
Phonon-dispersion curves and phonon-phonon interaction coefficients mediate the prediction.
Explicitly capturing complex phonon-phonon interactions and alloying effects leads to more accurate predictions of phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The method will predict phonon thermal conductivity values at least 10% lower than current predictions.
The method will achieve a mean absolute error below 0.5 W m^-1 K^-1.
The comparison baseline consists of empirical models or simplified computational approaches.
The method is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing up to ten principal elements.
The method is applicable at operating temperatures up to 1200 K.
Prediction accuracy may depend on the exchange-correlation functional, phonon-dispersion quality, and treatment of alloying effects.
TDTR can be used to measure phonon thermal conductivity at 300 K and 1000 K for the benchmark alloy set.
The hypothesis is falsified if prediction error exceeds 1.0 W m^-1 K^-1 for more than 20% of tested alloys.
